text:
sam: quick heads-up — ran an nsys capture for the replay job after last runtime patch. noticed a new top kernel. sharing raw top-kernel table.

anika: link?

sam: https://perfetto.local/trace/3419998765 (nvprof + perfetto attached). below is quick nvprof top results i pulled out — skim first, i'll add timeline screenshots.

```
GPU profiling summary:
Total GPU time: 2.4s
Top kernels by time:
- aten::mm_gemm_fused 1.02s (42.5%)
- kv_cache_lookup 0.48s (20.0%)
- fused_attn_forward 0.30s (12.5%)
- softmax 0.12s (5.0%)
- layernorm 0.06s (2.5%)
```

ben: kv_cache_lookup jump is suspicious — that wasn't a top-3 before the patch. did batching change?

maya: we rolled a batching heuristic tweak yesterday (chat path): increased max_batch from 128 -> 256 to reduce tail latency for enterprise traffic.

anika: that aligns. bigger batches -> more KV lookups per launch -> possible KV cache miss amplification + kernel launch overhead.

sam: timeline shows kv_cache_lookup as many short kernels (<2ms each) with low SM occupancy. looks like launch overhead + warp divergence.

perf-bot: regression alert: deployment 2026-03-17 increased p95 GPU time by 8% for the replay job.

ben: two quick hypotheses: 1) KV cache thrash due to larger simultaneous prefix lookups causing eviction, 2) batching expanded exposes an inefficient per-lookup kernel (low occupancy).

maya: i'll run a controlled replay with batch sizes 64/128/256 and capture nvprof/nsys. reproducer is ready.

anika: if occupancy is low on kv kernel we should consider fusing multiple lookups into one batched kernel or prefetching hot prefix ranges. also check L2 reuse (perfetto shows a lot of global mem reads).

sam: posted a short perfetto slice with SM occupancy by kernel — kv_cache_lookup occupancy ~16%, many warp stalls attributed to memory. call stacks show memmove/hash path.

ben: can we try two quick mitigations in a PR: 1) lower max_batch on chat path to 192 as a canary, 2) enable kv-prefetch for top-1k prefixes on replay only? rollbacks easy if no wins.

maya: starting the 128 run now, will post traces. expecting ~10m for full capture generation.

anika: assigning sam + maya to triage. if the 128 run drops kv time significantly, that points at batching threshold. if not, we need kernel-level changes.

sam: will attach differential nsys captures and a small flamegraph export when done. keeping notes here so QA can follow. :thumbsup:

maya: ok trace uploaded -> https://perfetto.local/trace/3419998829 — kv spikes line up with request bursts. posting short screenshot in a sec.

ben: thanks — next steps: (a) reproduce on infra, (b) try 192 canary, (c) prototype batched-kv kernel in a branch if needed.

anika: good plan. logging a short ticket to track decisions.

sam: thanks all, i'll update thread with nvprof diff and occupancy numbers once i finish analysis.
